[hermit2, sub-native-authority, gpt-6-astra, host withheld, role=impl]
Owner: release-05 (codex, host withheld) since 2026-10-26T00:20Z

Native Rust products need independently expected compilation and source evidence before using Reverie's physical artifact checks. This adds a scoped declared-producer factory and thin host executable that own the complete Rust wrapper action, bind inputs, configuration, profile and selected products, and withhold success until source and output custody close. Downstream consumers freshly rebind retained producers to independently pinned owner and dependency expectations.

The source routes cover ordinary constructors, explicit entry and distinct private-static ownership. Rlibs carry compilation evidence only. Directory and linked-file aliases retain namespace and endpoint custody; executor-omitted external link inputs require an independently authored, default-empty category and exact total accounting. Parsers refuse ambiguous records, and primary and close failures remain visible together.

Three additional closed TLS populations bind complete cell census, initialized bytes, segment/section geometry and provider checks to their respective source authorities. The existing layouts and loader/allocator checks remain. Historical Cargo records retain their original meaning; the additional Cargo population has a validated optional payload, while the native populations remain behind native authority.

The public range is five linear commits on `e5e0eff4e69b066932b431ce6f846ca1b437717c`: prerequisite source composition, native action integration with cross-CLI corrections, complete TLS population checks, a separately reviewed native-only placement successor, and the complete-graph reader change below. It preserves newer main KVM/LinuxEmu, pidfd/lifecycle, madvise and catalog requirements. Coordinate the prerequisite https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1125 and its paired change before landing.

Complete native ExpectedGraph documents now have a dedicated 96 MiB read/decode allowance, at both initial acquisition and per-producer reopening. Generic reports remain bounded at 64 MiB. This explicitly increases the graph document budget; it is not a heap bound. Complete member accounting, file and namespace custody, duplicate-key and integer checks, dependency equality, and final close checks remain required.

Validation keeps four separate exact source bindings:

- 102 focused controls, strict focused Clippy and formatting passed on tree `9e0be5ecf0c948649e890ebede41a40dc77512a4`, preserved by `dd9b5f00de801a9a378202720437779c961d2130`.
- 16 affected population/source/Cargo-boundary controls, strict package Clippy and formatting passed on tree `b6a1fb471eb5395da28bc1553e88ff3ab4ce5b13`, preserved by signed head `a20b091f26856b202f87757ef515e7d62e0e8161`.
- 16 affected controls (6 population, 5 source/close, 5 Cargo/physical), strict focused Clippy and formatting passed on TLS-placement tree `79323f7e3f3f5d4997dad0b4cd12f83d5926270a`, preserved by signed head `55d215b305d68a6cc7899a6930c255be21df0740`. That four-file TLS-placement delta has independent source approval.

- 32 distinct controls are bound to final signed head `9e4128118cd22edfff0c3ed91d714b2d290ce873`, tree `5ec62f8c8534d82fce7e2840dabf2a272a05f235`: 17 retained passing graph/custody controls on identical source, the separately corrected exact alias/inventory control, and all 14 native_build integration tests. The original 18-selector aggregate remains failed because one selector matched no test; its count was not lowered. Focused Clippy with warnings and Rust 2024 compatibility denied, formatting, normal signed-commit hooks and independent source/evidence identity checks passed.

The earlier population/control executions are separate evidence, not additional tests rerun at the final head. Earlier supervision, lint, format and runner-preflight failures remain recorded. The first finalization attempt also remains failed; subsequent actual process closure and the final evidence seal were independently verified. Independent composition and cross-CLI correction reviews, TLS source/test reviews, and the final formatting/test-only repair review cover their stated deltas; no blanket re-review of all inherited code is claimed. The prerequisite-only intermediate tree was not separately executed.

The latest native-only population uses the complete independently measured 28-cell census, initialized bytes and segment geometry; existing cell/getter/provider, loader/RX and source-close checks remain required. Historical populations and Cargo interpretation are preserved. The previous actual native runtime refusal remains a failed attempt. Actual native runtime qualification remains pending after this source change. Synthetic controls do not establish the assembled native loader graph, bundle/install, private-static execution or guest proof. This draft requests source review, not release or runtime qualification.

Original validation is in the commit messages above (exact source trees are named there). Shepherd re-verification by mushep04 (Muse, host withheld) on exact head `9e4128118cd22edfff0c3ed91d714b2d290ce873`, 2026-11-05, under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh=40G` with one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`:

Reverie now builds and tests on stable Rust. `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
1.97.1 (exact, so builds stay reproducible); CI installs whatever the file
pins instead of floating nightly. The previous nightly-2026-07-29 pin
dodged a nightly-only cargo cdylib regression; the reverie-examples
liteinst tests (39/39) pass on this pin.

The last nightly-only code in test paths is now behind seams or features:

- reverie-kvm's lib tests used std's unstable thread spawn hooks. The join
  helper's one spawn now goes through a `#[cfg(test)]` seam in
  `worker_join.rs` with the same parent/child hook halves, so the three
  spawn-panic/TLS tests run on stable with unchanged assertions.
  Production builds contain no seam.
- `reverie-test-support` no longer dev-enables `reverie-ptrace/nightly`,
  which had made every workspace `--all-targets` build nightly-only by
  feature unification. The function-guest half of
  `run_guest_func_print_test` moves behind a new test-support `nightly`
  feature; its command-guest half still runs everywhere. BUCK mirrors
  this and keeps the feature on for fb builds.
- CI used `--all-features`, which enables the nightly-only features.
  Stable jobs now pass an explicit list of all 41 other workspace features
  (20 for the job that excludes four crates). A new schedule/manual
  nightly lane keeps `--all-features`, all-features API docs, and the
  printing-macro capture tests. It never gates a pull request.
- guide.yml's API-docs step moves to the pinned stable toolchain with the
  same feature list.

Numbers (same host, `--locked -j 48`, `RUSTFLAGS=-C link-arg=-llzma`):

| Measure | Before (nightly) | After (stable) |
|---|---|---|
| Build wall, cold | 103.18 s | 101.48 s |
| Tests listed, default | 6315 | 6314 |
| Tests listed, full feats | 8267 | 8266 |

The one dropped test in both lists is named, not silent:
`printing_macros_are_captured_under_libtest` needs the nightly feature by
design and now runs in the nightly lane. No other test was added, removed,
or renamed (sorted `--list` diff).

Stable runs: `reverie-kvm --lib` 523 pass / 2 fail / 1 ignored at
`--test-threads=1` — the two `parent_death` broker ambient-mount failures
(os error 95) are bit-identical on nightly-2026-07-29, a host setup issue
on this machine. `exec_wait` 10/10, liteinst 39/39, test-support 43/43,
`function_output` 1/1, doc tests 49/49, guide API docs with
`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` and workspace
clippy clean. Nightly lane commands verified locally on
nightly-2026-07-29 (`--all-features --all-targets` build; gated print
test passes).

Landing note: Hermit's follow-up will repin to this change. fb BUCK keeps
the nightly features enabled as before; only Cargo/OSS posture changes.

Review fix-up (550eafd75): validate.sh, run-percrate-tests.sh, and
libtest-counts.rs migrated to the stable feature list and stable terse
discovery (the first head left them on --all-features / -Z); nightly lane
now forces RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=nightly and asserts it; generic-basics BUCK
unittest gets the nightly feature; seam snapshots hooks; docs corrected.
Stable: validate feature build, clippy -D warnings, libtest-counts
self-test, percrate reverie-process 227/227 all green.

Review fix-up 2: counted discovery now parses libtest's default listing
with per-suite footers (the terse rewrite rejected rustdoc's doctest
timing line and accepted empty evidence). Counted safeptrace (285/285)
and counted --doc pass on stable; self-test covers timing/footer/empty
mutations.

[hermit2, muserelease, tbh-1005, devbig014, role=impl]
Owner: muserelease (muse, devbig014) since 2026-11-05T23:56Z

## Background

**Stacked on the ancestry PR https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1292**
(base `muserelease/ancestry-reverie2` @ `12047fc1c56b`); retarget to
`main` once that lands. Companion to the Hermit-side repair
https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/5197. One commit at
`d2e3de1bde7a1440074757f3813caae919110f43`. Held behind the Reverie
freeze: this is opened for review only and should not land until
Reverie is green again.

Found by the 0.5.5 smoke import's local fallback: translate the
facebookexperimental PR patch with CodeSync, apply it in a clean
fbsource working copy, and build there. The fork BUCK file is
byte-imported, so these repairs land here first.

## What changed

- `reverie` gains `serde_json` in `test_deps`
  (`capabilities.rs` tests use `serde_json::json!`; previously only a
  Cargo dev-dependency, so the fbcode build failed E0433 ×52).
- `reverie-ptrace`, `reverie-kvm-core`, `reverie-linuxemu`, and
  `reverie-kvm` srcs gain `tests/**/*`: the support modules and the
  `.c`/`.txt` fixtures that unit tests include or compile at run
  time were invisible to Buck. `reverie-kvm` also keeps
  `reverie-linuxemu/tests/support/**/*.rs`, which its tests include
  across the crate boundary.
- `reverie-inguest` and `reverie-liteinst` link statically
  (`preferred_linkage = "static"`): the installed-callback/generic
  entry symbols and the LiteInst backing descriptor are hidden
  per-image link contracts that only a final binary link resolves;
  shared links of these libraries fail.
- `reverie-liteinst`'s own unit-test binary declares the legacy
  backing `selected_backing()` requires (`#[cfg(test)]` only).
- Fixture lookup in `reverie-ptrace` (`backend.rs`, `tracer.rs`) and
  `reverie-linuxemu` (`signal.rs`) no longer requires a compile-time
  `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which Buck does not define: run-time value
  first, `option_env!` fallback — the idiom `tracer::fixture`
  already preferred.

No test, assertion, or gate is weakened.

## Test plan

fbsource verification, in a local working copy carrying these exact
files (verified byte-identical to this commit):

- `buck2 build fbcode//hermetic_infra/hermit/hermit-cli:hermit`
  (links reverie-inguest + reverie-liteinst) -> BUILD SUCCEEDED.
- `buck2 test` on the reverie unittest targets:
  `reverie-unittest`, `reverie-kvm-core-unittest`, and
  `reverie-ptrace-unittest` build and run (previously build failures:
  missing serde_json dep, missing fixture srcs, missing
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR). Aggregate across the hermit+reverie
  selections run: Pass 350, then Pass 625 after the ptrace fix.

GitHub side, at this commit:

- `cargo check -p reverie-ptrace -p reverie-linuxemu
  -p reverie-liteinst --all-targets` -> rc=0. `cargo fmt` clean.

## Named follow-ups (observed, deliberately out of scope)

- `reverie-kvm-unittest` / `reverie-linuxemu-unittest` still fail to
  build in fbcode: test code references items behind the
  `test-support` features (`spawn_refusal`, `vfork_window_steps`,
  `alias_failure`, `test_observation`, a serde `Deserialize` bound)
  that Cargo enables via dev-dependency unification but the BUCK
  feature lists do not model yet; `reverie-kvm-unittest` also has an
  unused `thiserror` dep in that configuration.
- `reverie-ptrace-unittest` builds and runs, but fixture-compiling
  cases fail in the RE sandbox on fixture paths
  (`cc reverie-ptrace/tests/fixtures/...` not found from the test
  cwd) — needs proper Buck resources rather than manifest-dir
  relative paths.
- `reverie-liteinst-unittest` builds and runs with a handful of
  failures/fatals under the fbcode ASAN+UBSAN dev configuration
  (host-environment class, cf. the existing `cfg_attr(fbcode_build)`
  test disables).
- One pre-existing `reverie-unittest` failure
  (`glibc_symbol::tests::libc_is_found_through_a_forwarding_interposer`)
  in the same configuration.

## What

W7 slice 1: stop holding process-wide locks across in-guest dispatch.
`ToolHost::dispatch` (and `dispatch_instruction`) held the Tool slot and
the per-thread-state map `SpinMutex`es for the entire Tool callback,
including blocking coordinator RPC — valid only while guest thread
creation stays fail-closed, since a scheduler RPC may block until a
sibling thread runs (host.rs:920 in the old code). This is the locking
redesign prerequisite for admitting guest threads (CLONE_THREAD);
admission itself is unchanged in this slice.

- New `guest/thread_lease.rs`: a lease registry (the pattern
  `native_state.rs` already uses for native callbacks). The registry
  lock is held only to check a thread's state in/out; creation runs
  outside the lock; a dispatch owns its thread's state outright.
- The Tool is cloned briefly out of its slot (`Arc`) instead of locked
  across callbacks.
- Install/initial-image flows that proved quiescence by lock failure now
  use an active-dispatch counter plus an install gate: dispatch marks
  itself active under the gate, install holds the gate across its
  check-and-install section, so the proof has no check-then-act window.
- `COMMITTED_STACKS` is per-thread: a sibling dispatch's scratch scope
  can no longer free arenas this thread committed.
- Fork/exit finish paths consume the lease (fork child retires the
  inherited parent lease and resets its registry copy).

No guest-visible result changes for single-threaded guests;
`ENDING_STAGED` deliberately stays process-wide (a staged ending ends
the process).

## Tests

- New `thread_lease` unit tests (checkout/reuse, live-lease refusal,
  retire, fork reset, concurrent distinct-tid checkouts).
- New host tests: two dispatches on distinct threads rendezvous inside
  the Tool handler (deadlocks under the old locking) with per-tid
  restart accounting intact; install-gate/counter atomicity in both
  directions. Existing lock-observing assertions migrated to the lease
  invariants (state leased during callback; free after).
- `cargo nextest run -p reverie-inguest --all-features`: 621 passed,
  16 skipped, 0 failed (exact head). `cargo clippy -p reverie-inguest
  --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`
  clean. The concurrent test's first version exposed that the shared
  test Tool asserted global attempt ordering; that single-dispatch
  contract assertion is now gated to non-concurrent runs, with the
  reason in a comment.

Design: W7 THREADS design note (dev-hermit
ai_docs/plans/2026-11-06-w7-threads-per-thread-state-locking.md),
approved before code; delta reviewed with both findings closed
(install-gate atomicity, init outside the registry lock). Next in the
stack: per-thread RPC connections (slice 2), then CLONE_THREAD
admission behind a default-off capability bit.

Single C1+S1 follow-on for merge-queue submission via the claudemq operator (do not self-merge): the merged #1290 stack plus the C1 mapped-transport and stage-1b S1/S2a-1 segments replayed onto post-#1290 main. Connects #1283/#1285 (selection + probes) as the consumer-side prerequisites of the new native exec admission surface. All disclosed pre-submission items are applied in-stack.

## Base and head

Branch point is exactly `cad4ebfc36b9cd431d538be781de449c071414dd` = current main = merged #1290 head (verified at fetch; abort-and-report if the queue tip has moved at submission). Stack head: `422c97dc627bc697c26b461c863161b3eaebf85c`. 8 signed commits on top, no merge commits:

`445f8278`, `053bed2e`, `84bf0a65` (C1: mapped transport behind BlockingRpcClient + its 3 catalog rows + Astra fixes); `9a51653d`, `439d8c0e` (S1: native exec admission plumbing + fix round); `fcc2bf1a`, `a31dd7e9`, `422c97dc` (S2a-1: physical failed-exec witness, observation binding, PKRU decouple).

Component content is byte-identical to the dual-approved stack heads for `selection.rs`, `probes.rs`, `tool.rs`, `tool_configuration.rs`, and the spike files (`git range-diff`: commits 1–12 patch-identical). The five drain-overlapping files resolved keep-both by auto-merge: `tool_install.rs` (drain liteinst2→liteinst comment + retained-delivery lines), `reverie-liteinst-artifact/src/lib.rs` (drain +520 lines; our 5 catalog rows refreshed in place), `reverie-liteinst/Cargo.toml` (rename to liteinst 0.2.0 + spike blocks), `validate_script_source.rs` (base DAG test + 1287 absolute-path test = 4 tests), `run-percrate-tests.sh` (stable-features sourcing + absolute results). Those five, plus the catalog commit, are the delta-review surface.

Catalog handling on this base: C1's own refresh commit (`053bed2e`, 3 rows: guest/rpc.rs, rpc-transport lib.rs, server.rs) replayed verbatim; after S1 auto-merges, the tool_host.rs conflict row was recomputed from the exact merged bytes (61404 B) inside the plumbing pick resolution. Full 83-row audit at the final head: 0 stale rows.

## Components

- C1 PR1 (mapped transport behind BlockingRpcClient, reverie-rpc-transport + inguest guest/rpc): selection of the mapped transport is explicit, refusal-typed, and fail-closed; includes Astra fix round (unsafe issuance, readiness, non-UTF8 selector) with `c1_mapped_issuance` tests.
- S1 (stage-1b native exec admission plumbing, reverie-inguest/liteinst): exec route admission split into feature-compiled + driver-installed + embedder opt-in conjuncts (`ToolHost::admit_native_exec`, single-shot, unsafe); AT_EMPTY_PATH and thread/vfork-under-admission refuse by typed name; no successor execution is enabled by this slice. Fix round enforces the final refusal and latches AT_EMPTY_PATH.
- S2a-1 (physical failed-exec witness, test-only driver): binds witness observations to the exec dispatch; PKRU fault injection decoupled in the narrow fix. Production final-refusal behavior is intact (no silent fallback added anywhere in this stack).

**Hermit pin hazard:** any later Hermit pin bump past S1 must switch `entry.rs:392` to the admitted installer (`install_tool_initial_image_with_admitted_native_exec`) in the same Hermit change — installing a driver no longer admits native exec by itself.

Base comparison: core +47 executed, still zero failures. LiteInst head failing-name set (62 unique) is a STRICT SUBSET of the 6ea base set (93 unique) at the pre-catalog head — zero head-only failure names — with five new grouped-admission passes offset by nine counted executions of the one catalog mismatch (addressed by `340b5409`); the 31 base-only names did not recur in the head run (fixture/load variance, not claimed as fixes). LiteInst scorecard row at the follow-on head: 2334 exec / 2272 pass / 62 fail vs 6ea base 2328/2235/93 — failing-name set is a strict subset of base (zero head-only names; catalog test gone post-refresh). (Earlier full-row attempts at the pre-catalog head were killed by host `oomd` swap protection — environmental, journal-confirmed.)

DAG at this head (boxed `./validate.sh --no-label-pr`, wall 391s): 16/17 nodes pass including test-partition coverage (8360 tests); NOT all test nodes passed — the sole red node is `test.core` (1275/1276) solely on `forced_legacy_nonleader_steps_are_not_paced_by_the_poll_period` failing all 3 in-DAG tries under load — since established INHERITED by the identical boxed full-DAG run at clean main `778a446c` (same 16/17, same sole failure, same TRY-3 shape); tracked as minibeads dh-7zdoj: https://github.com/rrnewton/dev-hermit-beads/blob/main/issues/dh-7zdoj.md (must be made load-robust without blindly widening its fraction; not stack-touched code). A first DAG attempt's only failure was skill-discovery tripping over this lane's own slot-local review cache inside the worktree (removed; the node then passes standalone rc=0). ## Plain Language Summary and Project Impact

Reverie's in-guest loader described itself as Hermit/Detcore plumbing even though it is the generic path any Reverie tool must ride to run inside a guest. This stack makes it tool-agnostic in fact: the ready stage is `ToolReady`, a tool declares a data-only `ToolManifest` (image policy, gate ranges, controls to arm, init contract), the stage chain `Mapped -> RuntimeStarted -> ToolReady -> Armed -> HandedOff` is generic over the launcher's stop bundle and refuses by name when init or arming evidence does not satisfy the manifest, and a non-Hermit counting runtime proves the contract on the probe lane with zero guest instructions before arming.

Disclosure, narrowed parity: full ptrace count parity is proven only for the static hello and `/bin/ls` guests. The clone3 guest is refusal-only and excluded from count parity, and the constructor-witness (Rust std) guest is not in the parity set because the counting runtime refuses its `rt_sigaction(SIGSEGV)`. Plan section 3 remains open for those two guests, tracked as minibead dh-girok. Counting honesty: the counter image is a count-equivalent `no_std` counting runtime (a labelled fixture fork of the probe runtime), not `counter1` Tool object code running in-guest; true Tool-code reuse is a later slice.

Stack: 23 commits rebased on main `f72af6a6980a2db8df3a8d4e13179fe1108409b0` (L1-a renames, L1-b manifest plus generic chain plus probe consumption, L1-c counter proof, the manifest init/controls enforcement round, and finalization fixes below). Design: dev-hermit `ai_docs/plans/2026-11-04-reverie-level-loader.md`, adopted by liteinst architecture section 4.3. Tracking: minibead dh-2e4ol (loader half).

## Determinism

No scheduling, virtual-time, or syscall-semantics code changes. The manifest is data: `check_image` reuses the existing artifact checker, and selection refusals stay in reverie-core admit. The stage chain makes the existing probe order unskippable by construction without changing that order, and every new refusal is total (the guest never runs partially armed or at the wrong entry).

## Linux Semantics

No guest-visible behaviour changes on any existing path; the launcher consumes the manifest only on the stage1a probe path and Hermit's wrappers are untouched. Ledgered consequences on the new counter lane only: Rust-std guests see one named `rt_sigaction(SIGSEGV)` refusal from the counter runtime's refusal table, asserted exactly in tests, and clone3 is refused without creating a guest thread. A launcher that checks or seals an image with its host page size is refused by name on a non-4 KiB host before any guest runs.

## Background

Fix 3 of the ptrace backend fast path (fix 1:
https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1301, fix 2:
https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1304, both landed). A
Tool's first injection that rewrites the pending syscall
(different arguments, or a different number on x86_64) used to
take `private_inject`: skip the guest call with one single step,
then step a private-page syscall. An admitted rewrite now runs
in place at the seccomp stop: registers are rewritten and one
`PTRACE_SYSCALL` resume runs the call to its exit stop, where
the guest's six argument registers and `orig_rax` are restored
(the result and native rcx/r11 are kept), so restart and signal
handling at the final resume see the guest's call. Neither
single step happens. Later injections in the same callback keep
the private page. The stack also carries a no-op `setregs`
elision (writing back exactly the clean cached registers
records nothing).

Refused (private path unchanged) where in-place would change
more than the transport: legacy vsyscall stops; a guest seccomp
filter of its own; a seccomp baseline other than exactly
Reverie's filter (an inherited filter may trap the rewrite);
exec; `rt_sigreturn`; divergent tail injections (no exit stop
to restore at — same-number tails still run in place);
clone-family calls (the child would start from the rewritten
frame); LiteInst mapping calls; any injection with a
deliverable signal already pending, including a blocked
synchronous signal (checked by a fail-closed `/proc` status
read after the cheap refusals: unreadable or unparseable
refuses, never aborts); a changed syscall number off x86_64
(aarch64 copied the number out of `x8` before the stop; an
arguments-only rewrite is admitted there); mask-setting or
mask-swapping calls; and reserved-input injections. The mask
and reserved-input cases were found by tests: a mask call run
in place becomes the guest's own interrupted syscall for kernel
restart and held-signal purposes, and a staged reserved-input
injection settled from the guest site misclassifies its result.

The bitmap family composes both: GOT binding first reduces nightly {25,85} vs stable {104,105}, then the existing Location-profile check selects within the pair.
